scope: Proposition 5.8 (Obtaining the diagram clause) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose a finite-system scheme has the structural and presentation conditions of Definition 5.2, and is categorical at its eligible levels. For an unbounded supply after refinement, assume the eligible-subclass hypothesis of Convention 5.3. Either of the following inputs supplies the diagram clause, after the indicated closure refinements. 1. For each infinite σ, at all sufficiently large eligible levels, the relation of being sent to another list by an arrow is reversible on lists of cardinality at most σ, and their orbit sets have a bound depending only on σ and the fixed scheme. In this case take stabilization bounds and require enough smaller levels below the receiving level for the bounded arities in use. 2. Same-level arrows preserve isomorphism orbits of bounded lists, and comparisons of such orbits in well-ordered charts are independent of the eligible level. More precisely, for each arity, equivalence of two term patterns by an isomorphism in their respective charts is the same relation on patterns whenever both patterns are bounded at the levels under comparison. The componentwise exhaustion condition follows whenever arrows have only componentwise strong- ness as their additional structural content. For any other arrow condition its exhaustion assertion remains a separate obligation.
